source_text: In die quo convictus fuerit, reddet. Dilatio confessionis auget vulnus. Hodie si vocem eius audieritis.
orientation: Origen is applying the ram of the trespass offering to the soul's duty of confession, urging immediate response to God's voice.
pass_a_gloss: On the day on which he will have been convicted, he shall repay. The delay of confession increases the wound. Today if you will have heard his voice.

choices.why: Keeps the future perfect passive force of the Latin, indicating the moment of proven guilt as the trigger for repayment.
Preserves the future indicative with its command-like force in legal context.
Keeps the noun phrase structure and the glossary term 'confession'.
Literal rendering of the metaphor; the wound is the soul's sin-sickness.

choices.english: today if you will have heard his voice
choices.why: Keeps the future perfect in the protasis and the direct address, matching the Psalm quotation's urgency.
rejected: if today you hear his voice
today, if you hear his voice

pass_b_english: On the day he is convicted, he shall repay. Delaying confession only deepens the wound. Today, if you hear His voice (Psalm 94:7; Hebrew 95:7).

problems.why: 'eius' refers to God's voice, not the convicted person's. The Psalm quote means 'if you hear His [God's] voice.'
problems.fix: Today, if you hear His voice (Psalm 95:7).
problems.ruling: 'eius' in Psalm 95:7 refers to God (capitalized in liturgical Latin), not the convicted person; 'his' misleads readers about the source.

problems.why: LXX Psalm 94:7, not 95:7; Hebrew numbering differs by one.
problems.ruling: LXX/Vulgate Psalm 94:7, not 95:7; Hebrew numbering differs by one, misleading reference.

edits.old: Today, if you hear his voice (Psalm 95:7).
edits.new: Today, if you hear His voice (Psalm 94:7; Hebrew 95:7).

fixed: Changed 'his voice' to 'His voice' because 'eius' refers to God's voice in the Psalm quotation, not the convicted person's.
Changed 'Psalm 95:7' to 'Psalm 94:7; Hebrew 95:7' because the source follows LXX numbering, where this verse is Psalm 94:7, one behind the Hebrew numbering.

last_rejected.why: LXX Psalm 94:7 = Hebrew Psalm 95:7, but citation format is garbled and confusing.
last_rejected.ruling: Format correctly distinguishes LXX (94:7) from Hebrew (95:7); not garbled, just scholarly convention.
